_comment: Segment binding at the peasant seam — bestiary.Resolve(ref, WithInputFormat(InputFormatPeasant)), which is exactly what `bestiary show <ref>` passes. The corpus is driven HERE and not at a bare Resolve() on purpose: five of the six must-not-widen refs below are NOTFOUND at a bare Resolve() (auto-detect routes them to SchemeHuggingFace/SchemeRaw), so pinning them there would pin NOTFOUND->NOTFOUND and be vacuous. Each row pins its CANDIDATE SET, not merely its outcome class: `entities` is the sorted set of entity keys the candidate set spans (the identity-level candidate set, the granularity the acceptance criterion is written in), and `refs` is the sorted provider|id set, pinned for the must-not-widen rows where provider-level widening is the risk and deliberately left empty elsewhere. Roles: `repair` = a ref the fallback pass newly answers (was model-not-found before the segment-binding repair); `must-not-widen` = a ref that already resolved in the strict pass and must come back byte-identical, since a widened binding here is how a positional-parser repair silently breaks working lookups; `entity-view-guard` = a live entity key that must stay model-not-found at this seam, because `show` only reaches its aggregate entity view when model resolution misses — letting the fallback pass claim these keys is how a resolver-only sweep can hide a large CLI regression; `composition-witness` = a ref that is answerable only when TWO independent levers have both landed (the segment-binding repair and the gpt tier re-key), so it is red if either is absent; its preconditions additionally assert that no variant-empty artifact exists at the probed version and that the candidate set genuinely spans more than one identity.

provenance.ref: the amended unique-resolution arm of the segment-binding criterion: `ling/2.6` resolves uniquely to `ling@2.6#1t`

mutation.description: two segments, no provider prefix: the trailing version token lands in the VARIANT slot under positional binding and can never match a variant-empty entity, so the ref was unresolvable before the repair

provenance.ref: the same criterion's provider-qualified spelling: `ant/ling/2.6` resolves uniquely to `ling@2.6#1t`

mutation.description: the provider prefix is consumed by the pre-existing three-segment strip arm, leaving the same two-segment residue as the bare spelling — so both spellings must land on the same single identity, and the variant-carrying siblings at that same version must NOT be pulled in

provenance.ref: the criterion's scoped-ambiguity arm: `openai/gpt@5.1` returns ErrAmbiguous over exactly its openai-served candidates | 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: openai retired gpt-5.1-chat-latest and the three gpt-5.1-codex ids from its own provider row, leaving gpt-5.1 as the ONLY 5.1 id openai serves. The provider-scoped candidate set therefore collapses to one and the outcome is resolved, not ambiguous. The provider-equality guard this row was authored for is unchanged and still under test — it is what keeps the answer to openai/gpt@5.1 from listing the other hosts' 5.1 rows — and the scoped-AMBIGUITY arm is still pinned by anthropic/claude/4.6 and 302ai/claude/haiku@4.5.

mutation.description: the two-segment provider strip is guarded on the candidate's OWN Provider field, so the ambiguity is scoped to the named provider instead of every host of the family; an is-a-known-provider test would not do, since mistral/minimax/meta/google/openai are all known providers AND family-shaped tokens

provenance.ref: the criterion's `gpt/5.1` arm: an improvement from not-found to a correctly-scoped ambiguity over its groups, NOT a unique resolution | 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: a third 5.1 identity, gpt@5.1{fast}, now exists upstream, so the unqualified span is three entities instead of two. The pin widens with the catalog, not with the rule.

mutation.description: no provider segment, so no strip fires and the ambiguity spans every host of the family — the row exists to pin that the repair does not silently narrow an honestly-ambiguous ref to one provider

provenance.ref: the criterion's `openai/gpt/5.1` arm, over its groups | 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: a third 5.1 identity, gpt@5.1{fast}, now exists upstream, so the unqualified span is three entities instead of two. The pin widens with the catalog, not with the rule.

mutation.description: the three-segment strip arm carries no provider-equality guard (unchanged by this repair), so this spelling stays as wide as the bare one — pinned so a later tightening of that arm cannot land unnoticed

provenance.ref: the worked example behind the if/else form of the variant-empty version binding: an abort form loses thousands of resolvable refs of this shape

mutation.description: an explicitly named variant plus an @-suffix that is a VERSION rather than a date: the variant slot is already pinned, so the date-to-version rebind applies unconditionally here — a rebind rule that refused variant-carrying candidates outright would drop this ref

provenance.ref: the structural twin, verifiable today, of the deferred composition witness: a family+version whose artifacts are ALL variant-carrying resolves to a correctly-scoped ambiguity over those tier keys, not to not-found

mutation.description: the catalog holds no variant-empty `claude@4.6`, so the base-first preference finds nothing and the last-resort pass lets the rebound version segment reach the variant-carrying tiers; the ling rows above are the control that this pass never fires when a variant-empty artifact DOES exist

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a catalog id that IS literally `<vendor>/<family>`, the exact shape the two-segment provider strip could mis-read

mutation.description: resolves in the strict pass as an exact model id, so no repair rule may run at all — a rule that fired per-model rather than on a globally empty match set would widen this to every codestral host

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a vendor-prefixed catalog id served by four providers, where a widened binding would add rows from the bare-`sonar` family

mutation.description: the multi-provider case of the same shape: the pinned ref set is the whole point, since a widening here changes WHICH rows come back without changing the entity key. The pinned set is POST-CREATOR-FIRST: `sonar` is created by perplexity, whose earliest curated distribution surface present in the match set is `perplexity-agent`, so the single-group cross-provider branch narrows the four co-hosting rows (kilo, openrouter, perplexity-agent, vercel) to the creator-hosted one before returning. The outcome is still `resolved` on the same entity key, and no ambiguity listing is involved; the narrowing is the creator preference deciding WHICH single host `bestiary show` renders. This row therefore still fences widening — any extra row here, or any row from the bare-`sonar` family, is a real widening

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a family/variant ref whose single row carries a vendor-prefixed id unrelated to the ref's own segments | 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: nano-gpt began serving mercury-coder-small, so a SECOND provider row reaches the same entity and the outcome is ambiguous rather than resolved. The identity pin is unchanged (still exactly mercury/coder — the ref did NOT widen to another entity), and the ref set is re-pinned to both hosts so a rule-level widening still reddens.

mutation.description: the ref's segments and the resolved id share no prefix, so a binding change shows up as a different id rather than a different provider

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a family whose own name ENDS in a version-shaped token, the hardest case for any rule that re-reads a segment as a version

mutation.description: the digit `3` sits inside the family segment rather than in a slot of its own — a rebind rule that scanned for version-shaped tokens instead of using slot position would mangle this ref

provenance.ref: known falsifier: a hyphenated family whose LEADING token is also a live provider name (`xpersona`), the trap the two-segment provider strip is guarded against

mutation.description: the family segment begins with a provider name but is not equal to one, so the provider-equality guard must leave it alone; a prefix-based strip would delete `xpersona-` and lose the ref

provenance.ref: a pinned member of the entity-view set the criterion protects: `show llama@3.3#70b` must keep rendering its aggregate entity view

mutation.description: a bare, sized entity key with an @-suffix that is a version, not a date: this is exactly the shape an ungated date-to-version rebind swallows into model resolution, which silently costs the key its entity view — the rebind is gated on a provider segment having been stripped, and this key has none

provenance.ref: a pinned member of the protected entity-view set

mutation.description: the unsized, variant-empty spelling of the same trap: family plus an @-version and nothing else

provenance.ref: a pinned member of the protected entity-view set

mutation.description: the variant-carrying spelling: two segments plus an @-version, so both the variant-empty rebind and the date-to-version rebind must decline it

provenance.ref: a pinned member of the protected entity-view set

mutation.description: the identity-modifier spelling: the `{...}` segment is stripped before slot binding, so this key exercises the same trap with a modifier attached

provenance.ref: the composition witness of the segment-binding criterion: it is green only when the gpt tier re-key AND the binding repair have both landed, and red if either is absent | 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: the span widens 6 -> 9 entities and 6 -> 10 refs, all of it upstream movement rather than any change to the rule. A {fast} tier now exists for all three tiers (vercel's -luna-fast / -sol-fast / -terra-fast rows), openrouter's three -pro rows moved to kilo, and kilo's new openai/gpt-5.6-sol-discounted row joins gpt/sol@5.6 through the exact-ID pin that reads "discounted" as a pricing attribute rather than identity — without that pin it minted a bare gpt@5.6 that absorbed this whole query and collapsed the scoped ambiguity to a single kilo rehost.

mutation.description: REPLACES the deferred slot this row was authored as. The 5.6 tiers are now variants of family `gpt`, so this ref names a real (family, version) pair with several identities under it and comes back as a correctly-scoped ambiguity instead of model-not-found. Two measured facts are pinned that a summary would lose. (1) The scope is SIX entities, not three: the criterion's listing predates the -pro pins, and each tier at 5.6 carries a base key and a {pro} key, both honest candidates for a ref that names neither. (2) The candidate ref set is ONE row per entity identity, which is why openai's `gpt-5.6` stands for gpt/sol@5.6 while its sibling spelling `gpt-5.6-sol` does not also appear — pinning the ref set is what makes a widening of WHICH rows come back visible here. No base `gpt@5.6` artifact exists and no upstream row would produce one; the role precondition asserts that, so this row can never be read as a claim that one does. It required NO resolver change: the binding repair alone carries it once the keys exist.
